header: THE DOCUMENT MODEL OF THE "DOWNLOAD AS PDF" OF AN EXECUTIVE DEEP SYNTHESIS (EDS) REPLY. The reply is structured data (headline, overview, findings, tables, charts, sources), so I DRAW the PDF from that data (vector text and vector charts, selectable and searchable), never a screenshot of the screen. This file turns the reply into print-ready blocks: text runs with their script (so each run gets a font that has its glyphs), table cells in the same reading as on screen (rate / approver / note), chart geometry (already scaled), the sources and the file name. I keep it pure: no I/O, no PDF library, no clock (the caller passes `now`), so every rule is tested (edsPdfModel.selftest.ts). edsPdfDocument.tsx only paints what this model says.

symbols.name: PLAIN
doc: These are the characters the embedded fonts do not have; I write them the plain way. Everything else the replies use - ₹ × – — • ° ½ and curly quotes - is in the fonts.

symbols.name: EMOJI
doc: The fonts cannot draw emoji (the on-screen "✅" and friends), so I remove them and never show an empty box.

symbols.name: splitScripts
symbols.sig: export function splitScripts(text: string): Array<{ text: string; script: Script }>
doc: I split text into runs of one script each. The Hindi and Bengali fonts hold only their own script (no space, digit or ASCII punctuation), so a space, an ASCII digit or a punctuation mark is always drawn in the main font: "सेल स्थापना" is the word "सेल", a space, and the word "स्थापना". A zero-width joiner stays inside its word (it takes part in shaping).

symbols.name: inlineRuns
doc: Here I turn the inline markdown of a finding or paragraph (**bold**, *italic*, `code`) into runs, with rupee grouping and plain symbols, each run split by script.

symbols.name: plainOf

symbols.name: PDF_BODY_WIDTH_PT
doc: I keep a table in one block (it moves to the next page whole, with its heading) only if it FITS on a page. The painter used to decide that by the number of rows (12 or fewer), but an 11-row table whose rows wrap to 3 or 4 lines is taller than a page, and the PDF library then draws the page on top of itself. So I estimate the height here, from the text and the column widths, on the generous side: a table judged too tall only runs on over the page break (its heading row repeats), which is always safe; one judged short enough must really fit.

behaviours: ≥ ≤ → ≈ are written plainly
emoji and zero-width marks are removed (never an empty box)
the rupee sign, ×, dashes and curly quotes are kept (the fonts have them)
a rupee sign is a run of its own, the number after it is latin
each Hindi word is a devanagari run; the spaces between are in the main font (the Hindi font has no space)
Bengali words and Bengali digits are bengali runs; quotes and spaces are latin
a zero-width joiner stays inside its Hindi word
no characters are lost or changed by splitting
bold, italic and code runs
rupee amounts get the Indian digit grouping, '/-' stays
the markers themselves are not printed
first column is a label
'Not stated in circular' / N/A / Nil are 'none' cells
rate + approver: the approver is its own line
a [condition] becomes a note under the approver
a bracket that is not an approver is a note, not an approver
a bare amount gets Indian grouping and keeps decimals
a year is not an amount
an empty condition '[]' is nothing
column widths: the first 28%, the others share the rest
a table's sources are the archive's names
a source is named by its label, else the year, else 'Source'
niceTicks start at 0 and end at or above the maximum
slicePath draws a full circle as a closed path (no zero-length arc)
pie: percentages sum to 100 and carry the unit
pie of zeros is not drawn
bar: the longest bar is 100% wide and the others are in proportion
bar: two series are named, one series is not
line: every point lies inside the drawing area, later points to the right, a larger value higher up
line: a single point is drawn, not divided by zero
scatter without a second value is not drawn
scatter points lie inside the drawing area
kpi: values are formatted with the unit (paise shown for all when one has them)
a chart without items is not drawn; a timeline keeps its order and numbers
file name: ASCII, no spaces, dated
a long title is cut between words, never in the middle of a word or a year
a title with no ASCII letters falls back to 'Briefing'
the question is trimmed and kept on one line
generated time is in IST
two paragraphs, one finding (an empty one is dropped), a source that does not exist is dropped from its chips
an empty second table and a chart with nothing to draw are left out
sources are numbered, with a display date (no time zone shift)
abbreviations are carried
no question given -> no question block
hasPdfContent: a reply with content yes; an error, an empty reply and null no
the PDF button is used by the EDS reply (ExecutiveBriefing) and by nothing else
the button is drawn only when the reply has content
only the painter imports the PDF library statically
the button loads the PDF code on the click, not at page load
the library, the painter and the fonts are dynamic imports
the asked question is handed to the EDS reply (it is printed in the PDF)
font file ${f} is shipped
the Indic fonts are also registered as italic (upright files), so an italic paragraph with Hindi or Bengali cannot stop the PDF
Bengali is drawn in Baloo Da 2 (the PDF library mis-shapes conjuncts such as স্ক in Noto Sans Bengali)
the page style has no lineHeight (it would hide the footer)
the footer is fixed and carries the page number
the line height is set on every text (not on the page, not on a wrapper View: that spaced the text out)
the footer says the language model behind the EDS search summarised the circulars for convenience, and that the circular is the authority; it does not say the app was built by AI
the footer's page number uses the library's own Text (a render text with ANY line height is dropped)
a text inside a text (the runs of a paragraph, the reference tags) carries no line height of its own: it compounds and spaces the text out
a reference tag starts with ONE space (two made the library put a hyphen at the end of the line)
the Sources heading travels with the first source (never alone at the foot of a page)
11 rows of long text in 4 columns are taller than a page body, so the table is NOT kept as one block
a short table is kept whole
a table of 40 short rows is not kept whole either
the painter decides by the estimated height, not by the number of rows
a table too tall for a page STARTS ON A NEW PAGE (break), so the library cannot leave its repeated heading row alone at the foot of the previous page
the penalty amounts stay in the value; only the condition is a note; no approver chip
a clause reference such as 5(Xii) is one text, drawn plain (not as a bold value with a note)
a successful download shows no toast of ours (the browser's save window is the confirmation)
a failure still tells the person, so a broken download is never silent
